selectionReason: RC55 rejected a single first-160-cycle fade coordinate under fixed stress. RC56 therefore tested whether later capacity shape contains a stable within-condition ordering signal and audited an independent dense-capacity source without opening its cell-level outcomes.
newFacts: The official Aurora ZIP contains 797 entries: 199 metadata JSON, 199 BDF CSV, 199 BDF Parquet, and 200 other entries.

All 199 metadata files identify graphite negative electrodes, while 32 explicitly identify a LiFePO4 positive-electrode formula. The primary paper describes 36 long-term LFP/graphite cells, leaving four cohort members unresolved at the archive-metadata boundary.
No Aurora BDF cycling entry, cell capacity, or cell EOL value was opened or observed.

On opened RWTH data, R2 recent log-capacity slope reached blocked concordance 0.702128 and R3 normalized capacity level reached 0.723404; both kept one coefficient sign across all twelve leave-start-batch-out fits.
R2 and R3 supplied only 47 non-tied within-held-batch comparable pairs, below the registered minimum of 60, so no coordinate earned independent testing.
Python and dependency-free Node implementations selected no candidate, matched every gate and sign, matched all concordances exactly, and differed in full-cohort beta by at most 1.1661e-8.

H56-0.claim: No currently registered capacity coordinate and independently traceable cohort jointly support a transport claim.
H56-0.reason: Every capacity candidate missed at least one gate, and the candidate archive did not reconcile the paper's 36-cell LFP cohort.

H56-1.claim: One of eight registered R1-R3 capacity level, slope, or curvature coordinates stably orders remaining life across start batches.
H56-1.strongestSignal: R3_capacity_level, concordance 0.723404, 47 comparable pairs, stable coefficient direction
H56-1.consequence: Preserve the signal as method-development evidence; do not call it validation and do not use it to open Aurora outcomes.

H56-2.claim: The official Aurora archive exposes an exact, outcome-blind cohort of at least 36 same-condition LFP/graphite cells for independent transfer testing.

minimalAcademicAdvance: Later capacity level and local slope are more promising than one early fade scalar, but sparse EOL rounds can make a seemingly strong concordance statistically ineligible. RC56 also turns paper-to-archive cohort reconciliation into an explicit prerequisite for outcome-blind battery validation.

mostPromisingNextPath.hypothesis: A later, dimensionless capacity coordinate can transport ordinal cell frailty if endpoint resolution and cohort lineage are repaired before target outcomes are opened.
mostPromisingNextPath.differentCombination: Combine machine-readable cohort lineage, blocked rank validation, and an adaptive measurement schedule that densifies full-capacity checks only near each cell's estimated knee while keeping the final 80% crossing rule independent of the estimator.
mostPromisingNextPath.exactBottleneck: Signal strength, endpoint pair count, and target-cell lineage currently fail as separate prerequisites.
mostPromisingNextPath.firstDecisiveAction: Ask the Aurora authors or repository curator for an official mapping between the 36 paper cells and the 32 explicit LiFePO4 metadata records, without requesting cell-level outcomes. In parallel, quantify how a 50-cycle or adaptive RPT schedule changes expected non-tied pair count in a future same-condition batch.
mostPromisingNextPath.successSignal: An official one-to-one cohort manifest plus a prospectively frozen target design expected to yield at least 100 comparable pairs; only then seal one coordinate and open target cycling data.
mostPromisingNextPath.rejectionAndStop: If the cohort cannot be reconciled, do not use Aurora for confirmation. If prospective timing still cannot meet the pair budget, stop capacity-only ranking and move to an orthogonal, independently repeatable expansion, pressure, acoustic, or excitation observable.
mostPromisingNextPath.failureValue: Failure isolates whether the next investment belongs in data lineage, endpoint sampling, or new sensing rather than model complexity.

unverifiedClaims: The identity and reason for the four-cell difference between the paper's long-term cohort and explicit archive metadata remain unknown.
Whether R3 capacity level transports across chemistry and cell format remains untested.
Whether an adaptive RPT schedule preserves degradation dynamics while increasing pair resolution requires prospective validation.
safetyEthics: Only public historical battery metadata and previously opened RWTH capacity results were processed. Aurora cycling outcomes remained closed. No physical cell test, personal data, cyber experiment, safety decision, or deployment occurred.
nextCycleStart: Resolve Aurora cohort lineage without outcome access and build a prospective endpoint-pair budget for dense or adaptive capacity checks. Do not select another RWTH feature or open Aurora BDF data unless a new precommit has an exact cohort, an earned coordinate, and sufficient pair power.
